title: KV buffer offset overwrite caused by dynamic kernel handoff in tiled-attn path
creator: Maya Chen
description: After landing the tiled-attention micro-tiling and dynamic kernel handoff optimizations, we observed rare correctness regressions for long-context generation workloads (>= 16k). Outputs show silent numerical drift and token-level divergence that accumulates over long sequences. Investigation points to out-of-band writes into the KV buffer when the runtime switches from single-piece prefill kernels to tiled decode kernels under high concurrency and mixed-precision blending. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, repro artifacts, immediate mitigations, and a tested fix path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Checkout runtime-2.4 branch with tiled-attn and dynamic-kernel-selection enabled (flags: --enable-tiled-attn --dk-handshake=on).

2) Start a multi-worker serving instance with 3 GPUs, model: gptx-16k-fp16-quant (context 16384), batch mix: many small prefill requests + 1 long prefill (length 12k) followed by concurrent decode streams.
3) Send a long-context generation prompt that exercises cache reuse (e.g., repeated prefix + appended new content) and enable deterministic sampling (top-k with fixed seed).
4) Observe divergence: token 1024-1500 shows mismatched logits compared to baseline without tiled-attn. Re-run with logging enabled (KV_INDEX/DEBUG) to capture offsets.
5) Repro rate observed ~1 in 250 runs in cluster stress tests; increases when prefill-to-decode handoff coincides with high kernel-switch churn.
6) Local constrained reproducible test harness included in /playgrounds/kv-repro/ with run_repro.sh and a saved model snapshot (sha:abc123).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: race between kernel handoff and async KV write completion leads to stale write landing at earlier buffer offset (address reuse).

Memory analysis shows two workers using the same physical page group for KV chunks when handoff happens within the same allocation slab; allocator does not always fence writes across kernel group boundaries.
Reproduced locally with instrumentation: toggling ON the 'force_fence_on_handoff' flag eliminates repro (0/1000 runs), indicating missing memory fence/ordering is causal.

FP32 vs FP16: numerical drift magnitude larger with mixed-precision blending because smaller quantized blocks are more sensitive to small misplacements in KV indices leading to downstream softmax differences.
Concurrency pattern: high-frequency micro-batching ramps up allocator slab reuse which amplifies window for overlapping async device->host copies and kernel launch reorderings.
Relevant subsystems: kernel_selector, allocator/kv_slab, async_copy_executor, tiled_attn codepath, decode scheduler.
Observed that fallback path (single-kernel decode) bypasses the handoff and does not reproduce.
Heap/Slab metadata corruption not observed; corruption limited to stale/incorrect offset writes rather than buffer overflow or out-of-bounds.
Cross-check with valgrind-style memory tools on CPU harness is noisy; best visibility comes from device-level tracking and deterministic logging of KV-index writes.
Found a low-probability ordering: Kernel A schedules async copy( chunk X ), kernel B assumes chunk X free and issues write to chunk X before copy completes -> stale overwrite.
root_cause: Allocator slab reuse combined with missing ordering/fence between async device transfers and kernel handoff. The dynamic kernel selection path can cause two kernel groups to issue overlapping writes to the same KV chunk index without a synchronization barrier, producing offset mismatches and subtle numerical drift when mixed-precision tiled attention reinterprets the overwritten chunk.
mitigations: 1) Hotfix: enable conservative fencing on kernel handoff (force_fence_on_handoff=true) in runtime config for all customer-facing clusters running runtime-2.4. This avoids races at the cost of ~1-3% tail latency increase.
2) Emergency patch: allocator will mark recently-allocated chunks as 'quarantined' for N ms after async copies and avoid reusing identical slab pages until safe.
3) Add runtime telemetry to count 'overlapping_kv_writes' and log per-request stack trace when detected to aid triage.
4) Notify SRE + Customer Success for high-usage tenants (internal list) to opt-in to hotfix rollout.
5) Rollback tiled-attn dynamic handoff via feature-flag for impacted clusters if high error rates observed.
6) Add a deterministic unit test that simulates allocator race windows using injected delays to prevent regression.
proposed_fix: Implement a two-part fix: A) update async_copy_executor to expose a completion fence API and ensure kernel_selector invokes a fence before reassigning slab pages to a different kernel group; B) allocator changes to include per-chunk generation counters and compare-on-write to reject stale writes (and log). Include e2e test harness and perf benchmarks to measure latency impact. Target is to land fix in runtime-2.4.1 with regression tests.
